help.title: ScreenRec Help
help.description:
ScreenRec — a local desktop screen recorder.

RECORDING
Choose a source, output folder, frame rate, quality, and filename options, then click Start recording. Stop recording from the main window or the tray.

SOURCES
Monitor records the selected display. Screen region records a rectangle selected with the mouse. Application window captures a selected window. Browser tab uses the local Chrome/Edge extension and a one-time connection code.

AUDIO
You can record microphone audio, system audio, both, or no audio. Select devices and adjust the audio bitrate in the recording configurator.

FORMATS
MP4 is a broadly compatible choice. MKV is useful for resilient recording. WebM is suitable for web workflows and may use more CPU. Video quality and FPS affect image quality, CPU load, and file size.

OVERLAYS
The overlay editor can add an image and/or text. Move and resize each element on the frame preview, then set opacity, font, size, and color. Saved templates can be reused.

CATALOGUE
The Recordings tab lists completed videos. Search and sort files, select a recording, play or pause it, seek, change speed and volume, take a snapshot, use fullscreen, or delete it after confirmation.

TROUBLESHOOTING
If no monitor or window is listed, click Refresh sources and check that the target is visible. For a region, select an area at least 2 × 2 pixels.

If audio is missing, select the correct microphone or system device, enable the required audio mode, and check the bitrate.

If a browser tab does not connect, start a tab session in ScreenRec, install/load the extension, use the current connection code, and check that the browser allows capture.

If playback fails, verify that the file is complete, the format is supported, and the file is not still being recorded. If a folder cannot be opened or saved, check its permissions and available disk space.
